steps.description:
The program should run forever and can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.


The "Display Text" option on the LCD block allows you to enter a text. It also allows you attach certain sensors so that you can see the value sent out by a sensor. To do that, you need to use the "create text with" block to convert the sensor value to a text for the LCD to display. 


Using the LCD, display the value of a button sensor. 

1. What value do you see when the Button is not pressed?
2. What value do you see when the Button is pressed?

 

Hint:

1. Create text with
2. Use Forever Loop.

The program should run forever and can only be terminated when the Stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.


Show that your robot can perform the following with 1 Button:

1. When a Button is not pressed, a buzzer sound will be played.
2. When a Button is pressed and held, no sound will be played.


Hint:

1. Use logic to check for Button press.
2. Use Forever Loop.

The program should run forever and can only be terminated when the Stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.


Show that your robot can perform the following with 1 Button:

1. When a Button is not pressed, a fast beeping tone will be played.
2. When a Button is pressed and held, no sound will be played.


Hint:
1. Use logic to check for Button press.
2. Use Forever Loop.

The program should run forever and can only be terminated when the Stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.


Show that your robot can perform the following with 1 Button:

1. When Button is pressed and held, A4 note will be played.
2. When Button is not pressed, C4 note will be played.


Hint: 
1. Use logic to check for Button press.
2. Use Forever Loop.

The program should run forever and can only be terminated when the Stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Without stopping the program, the volume of the buzzer sound should vary with the pressing of buttons.

Show that your robot can perform the following with 2 Buttons:

1. When Button A is pressed and held, an A4 note will be played.
2. When Button B is pressed and held, a C4 note will be played.
3. When no Button is pressed, no sound will be played.


Hint:
1. Use logic to check for Button press.
2. Use Forever Loop.

The program should run forever and can only be terminated when the Stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Without stopping the program, the volume of the buzzer sound should vary with the press of a button.

Show that your robot can perform the following with 2 Buttons:

1. When Button A is pressed and held, an A4 note will be played.
2. When Button B is pressed and held, a C4 note will be played.
3. When no Buttons are pressed, a beeping F4 note will be played.


Hint: 
1. Use logic to check Button press.
2. Use Forever Loop.
Create a flowchart of the previous step.
